# Data-Driven Vegetation Management Strategies

By Dana Lister, Data Science Lead, PyroGuard Analytics

In 2023, our team faced a daunting challenge: a utility client in the Sierra Verde region was overwhelmed by the sheer volume of vegetation encroaching on their power lines. Traditional line clearance efforts were reactive and resource-intensive, often missing critical risk areas. This experience underscored for me the transformative potential of data-driven vegetation management.

By integrating remote camera feeds with historical outage and weather data, we developed a risk-scoring model that dynamically prioritized sections of the grid. Areas with dense canopy growth, combined with high wind forecasts and past fire incidents, received higher clearance priority. The model was tested over six months, leading to a 35% reduction in vegetation-related outages compared to the previous year.

My recommendation for utilities struggling with similar challenges is to move beyond static schedules and invest in analytics platforms that fuse diverse data streams. Prioritizing based on quantifiable risk enables targeted resource deployment, reducing costs and enhancing safety. The key is not just collecting data but deriving actionable insights that align with environmental and operational realities. With wildfire seasons growing longer and more intense, embracing these data-driven approaches is no longer optional—it is essential for resilience.
